headline: JPMorgan’s European Hub Takes Its Time Reporting Suspicious Money, Setting a German Fine Record
deck: Germany’s financial watchdog issued its largest anti-money-laundering penalty ever — €45 million — for twelve months of delayed suspicious-transaction filings. Measured in parent-bank earnings, the record lasts about a workday.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Germany’s all-time record BaFin AML fine (€45M / ~$49M) equals less than half a day of global parent net income, with zero executives charged.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Failing to declare €1,650 ($1,800) in restricted customs cash at Frankfurt Airport
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate confiscation and administrative fine representing a material share of an individual’s annual income

sources.title: BaFin Imposes €45 Million Administrative Fine on J.P. Morgan SE for Delayed Suspicious Transaction Reports
